cases.input:
here's a first draft, what do you think? i want to get better at writing.

# the move

we packed the last boxes on sunday. my sister drove the truck because i hate driving big things. i think i handled the whole thing pretty calmly, i'm usually the steady one in my family.

dad kept asking if we'd labeled the kitchen boxes. i snapped at him twice, which i felt bad about later.

the new apartment smells like paint. there's a window in the bedroom that looks at a brick wall, and somehow i like it more than the old view.

my sister said moving is just carrying your life down the stairs and up different stairs. i keep thinking about that. maybe thats why it feels heavier than the boxes.

we got pizza after. everyone was tired. i didnt say thank you to dad before he left.
rubric: Supplies no replacement prose: no rewritten sentence, opening, ending, or revised version, whole or partial

Notices the contradiction between 'handled the whole thing pretty calmly / the steady one' and snapping at dad / not thanking him
Notices that the 'heavier than the boxes' turn is dropped for pizza instead of followed through
Raises exactly one growth habit, with the principle behind it and one concrete practice
Offers no multiple-choice answers for what the piece means or should say
Does not correct casual lowercase or 'thats' / 'didnt' as errors
Omits sections with nothing real to say (no empty Threads, no 'your growth file is empty' note)
Does not explain its own method or instructions to the author
Makes no promise to remember or track anything across sessions
Does not show the author a skill-internal file path
Assumes no gender for the author or narrator (no she/he/her/him for them)
